passage: Chartres Cathedral, southwest of Paris, was rebuilt after a fire in the 1190s. The stained-glass windows made for the new building ______ form one of the most complete sets of medieval glass in the world.
question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.text: in the early thirteenth century the great majority of which survive
in the early thirteenth century, the great majority of which survive
in the early thirteenth century; the great majority of which survive;
in the early thirteenth century, the great majority of which survive,

explanation:
**Choice D is correct.** The clause "the great majority of which survive" is a nonessential supplement that interrupts the main clause, so it must be set off by commas on both sides.

**The Full Solution:**
- The main clause runs: "The stained-glass windows made for the new building in the early thirteenth century... form one of the most complete sets of medieval glass in the world."
- "The great majority of which survive" adds extra information about those windows; the sentence is complete without it.
- A supplement placed between a subject and its verb takes paired punctuation: a comma before it and a comma after it, as in choice D.

**Why the other choices are wrong:**
- A: With no punctuation at all, the supplement runs into the main clause, so "survive form" reads as a garbled pair of verbs.
- B: An opening comma without a closing one leaves the interruption unclosed, running the supplement straight into the main verb "form."
- C: Semicolons cannot set off a dependent "of which" clause; each semicolon would need an independent clause on both sides.
